anlatici: Turkish. Deadpan nature-documentary narrator observing the species 'junior developer' in its natural habitat. Warm low baritone, measured but brisk; bone-dry irony, zero emotion, never amused by his own lines. A tiny pause before the punchline, then moves straight on. Brisk, lively pace; do not drag.
deniz: Turkish. Young man, early twenties, a computer engineering student. Quick, conversational, self-deprecating; tired optimism with a small smile in the voice. Never whiny. Lands jokes by underplaying them. Brisk, lively pace; do not drag.
ozan: Turkish. Young man, the top student of the class. Precise, calm, slightly monotone and earnest; states sad facts as neutral data. No self-pity: the sadness is in the flatness. Brisk, lively pace; do not drag.
buse: Turkish. Young woman, bright, warm and fast; genuinely curious about people, friendly and never salesy. Smiles while talking. Brisk, lively pace; do not drag.
tolga: Turkish. Young man from Adana, laid-back and unhurried, with a light southern Turkish lilt (subtle, not a caricature). Surprised by nothing, amused by nothing; deadpan-cheerful. Brisk, lively pace; do not drag.
asuman: Turkish. Young woman, sweet, bubbly, sincere and polite; slightly posh but warm. Completely unaware of her privilege. Never sarcastic, never mean. Brisk, lively pace; do not drag.
